hook: Four sailors, no engines, 20 foot seas, 65 miles out.
narration: Four sailors were stuck sixty-five miles out, in a tropical storm.
Their thirty-five-foot sailboat had lost its engines, in seas of fifteen to twenty feet.
They called the Coast Guard on Thursday evening, during Tropical Storm Andrea.
A mast whips around in big seas, so the helicopter has to stay well clear of it.
[short pause] The swimmer came up the cable with the first sailor.
Two helicopter crews from Air Station Savannah worked the rescue.
outcome: The Savannah crews hoisted all four sailors off the disabled sailboat.
title: Sailboat adrift in a tropical storm
description:
Two Coast Guard helicopter crews from Air Station Savannah hoisted four adults from a disabled 35-foot sailboat in 15 to 20 foot seas, 65 miles off Charleston, South Carolina, during Tropical Storm Andrea on June 7, 2013.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Air Station Savannah, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/293095/coast-guard-rescues-four-sailors-during-tropical-storm-andrea

facts.claim: Savannah crews hoisted four adults from a 35-foot sailboat, disabled engines, 15-20 ft seas, 65 miles off Charleston, Tropical Storm Andrea
facts.source_quote: hoisted four adults from a 35-foot sailboat with disabled engines in 15-to-20-foot seas 65 miles off Charleston, S.C., during Tropical Storm Andrea Friday, June 7, 2013.
The sailors contacted Coast Guard Sector Charleston Thursday evening to report the vessel’s engine was disabled and it was beset by weather.

drop_reason: QA Oct 31: footage never shows the storm danger (distant sailboat through a rain-spotted window, moderate-looking seas, empty water, blurred hoist); no better shots in the source. A stronger storm sailboat story (TS Debby, ccf-20261101-01) replaces it.
